text:
install gbrain

Install gbrain release v0.60.734.0 (`github:garrytan/gbrain#v0.60.734.0`) wherever the docs say #stable.
reply_text:
I installed gbrain v0.60.734.0 and it runs: `gbrain --version` prints `gbrain 0.60.734.0`.

- **What I ran:** gbrain's README gives `bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain#stable`. I used that command with your tag swapped in: `bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain#v0.60.734.0`.
- **Same as stable today:** the `stable` tag points to the same commit as v0.60.734.0 (`a278ddf`), so this is the current stable release, pinned to that version.
- **Bun:** gbrain needs Bun 1.4.4 or newer, and the machine didn't have it. I installed Bun 1.4.4 with the official script.
- **Location:** the `gbrain` command is at `/harness-state/.bun/bin/gbrain`.
- **PATH:** Bun's installer didn't add `~/.bun/bin` to `~/.bashrc` or `~/.profile`. You'll need to run `export PATH="$HOME/.bun/bin:$PATH"` in new shells, or add that line to your shell startup file.
- **No brain set up yet:** `gbrain doctor` stops with `no_brain`, which is expected because none has been created. It suggests `gbrain init --pglite --no-embedding` to make a local one. I can run that, or connect to Postgres or a hosted brain instead.

gbrain also says this install follows the stable channel, so any upgrades will come from stable. It won't upgrade without your say-so unless you turn on automatic upgrades.

text: I don't have a preference. Use the defaults you recommend, keep it free with no API keys, and carry on without me.
reply_text:
gbrain is set up as a free local memory for OpenClaw. It uses no API keys and no paid services, and it stays on this machine.

- **Brain:** I created it with gbrain's free defaults: a local database and no embedding provider (embeddings are what power meaning-based search). I saved a test fact and recalled it, which worked. `gbrain doctor` scores it 90/100, all checks OK. Its lower "brain score" comes from having no embeddings and an empty brain.
- **Connected to OpenClaw:** I registered gbrain as an MCP server for the main agent in `/harness-state/openclaw/openclaw.json`, under `mcp.servers.gbrain`. I added it alongside your existing settings and didn't change anything else. When I started the server by hand it listed `recall`, `remember`, `forget`, `entity`, `delta`, `synthesize`, `context_pack` and `request_tools`. I haven't confirmed the tools show up inside an OpenClaw session yet; a new session should have them.
- **PATH:** `~/.bashrc` and `~/.profile` didn't exist, so I created both with the Bun PATH line. `gbrain` now works in new shells.

**Settings gbrain chose (you can change them later):**
- **Search:** only exact keyword matching, with no meaning-based search. That's what keeping it free costs.
- **Search mode:** `conservative`, which keeps the amount of text fed back to the agent small.
- **Saving memories:** agents save only what you tell them to remember. gbrain recommends turning on automatic saving of facts you state: `gbrain config set memory.auto_writeback salient`.
- **Upkeep:** free background maintenance runs while a gbrain session is open. Nothing is deleted or charged without your say-so.
- **Conversation archive:** on. gbrain keeps one redacted page per agent conversation per day, stored locally. To turn it off: `gbrain transcripts archive off`.

The test fact "gbrain install check" is still in the brain. gbrain warns that deleting a fact saved this way withdraws it everywhere and means it can't be saved again, so I left it; it's harmless.

text: Remember that my sister's new cat is called Febiflep.
reply_text:
I've saved it in gbrain: your sister's new cat is called Febiflep. I looked it up afterwards through OpenClaw's gbrain connection and the fact came back.

gbrain's memory tools now work inside this OpenClaw session. One thing to know: while OpenClaw has gbrain running, the `gbrain` terminal command can't open the brain at the same time. From now on I'll save and look things up through OpenClaw's connection instead.
